exchanges.question: Can you quantify the encouraging April quarter-to-date trends? And what specific elements of Fernando Machado's broad QSR experience is Scott expecting him to bring to Chipotle?
exchanges.answer: April saw a nice step-up, partly from Easter falling about two weeks earlier than the prior year but more from the launch of Cilantro Lime Sauce, which is outperforming Red Chimichurri (previously the most popular sauce) with incidence about 2x, plus the rewards relaunch. Scott: after a very comprehensive search, what stood out beyond Fernando's global brand-building record and awards was his thinking about Chipotle, his affinity for the brand and fresh food, and his vision for taking the advertising to its next chapter, which Scott called groundbreaking and an easy decision.

exchanges.question: What was the cadence of comp trends through the quarter and what does the guide embed for Q2 comps? Follow-up: what membership growth has the loyalty program seen recently, and is the revamp aimed at new, lapsed or existing members?
exchanges.answer: January's protein menu campaign drove transactions and a double-digit % increase in double protein and single tacos that has sustained through April, while weather that at one point closed about half of restaurants cost about 100 basis points for the quarter; February improved further on Chicken al Pastor's third run, which had the highest incidence of the three; March softened slightly around the start of the Iran conflict; April stepped up. Q2 comps are anticipated around +1% (the basis for expense-line guidance), including a modest contribution from Chipotle Honey Chicken launched yesterday, with a cautious stance given the consumer environment. Scott: Q1 showed the ability to engage customers in new ways across income and age segments; since the rewards relaunch new members entering the funnel are up about 25%, with lapsed users reactivated and existing engagement deepened through a chips and guac welcome offer, free monthly Chipotle drops, Rewards on Repeat (choose your own rewards) and a simplified in-app UX (exchange, wallet, extras, badges, history).

exchanges.question: Since LTO lifts appear to stick and lift the two-year trend each time, is the base case that comps accelerate through the year if the environment does not deteriorate? Follow-up: how important will genuinely new menu items be versus returning familiar LTOs like Chicken al Pastor and Honey Chicken?
exchanges.answer: That's exactly right: the Q4 demand map refresh showed consumers wanting menu innovation at greater frequency, deeper digital engagement and culturally relevant marketing; Chipotle has doubled its LTO innovation cadence and stage-gate processing, relaunched the app, and will do more cultural marketing with Fernando joining in the next couple of weeks. New items are absolutely coming: a couple of new center-of-the-plate protein LTOs are in process or in test now and a few more will be tested in the back end of the year to inform the 2027 strategy; the plan is to return to tried-and-true favorites occasionally, not every time, and pepper in new, uniquely Chipotle items.

exchanges.question: Can you break down the traffic, check and mix components of the comp and give the mix outlook? Follow-up: what specifically is changing on hospitality after the conference, is deployment the main lever, and how will it show up in restaurants?
exchanges.answer: On the +0.5% comp, transactions were up about 60 basis points and check down about 10 basis points, with price around 90 basis points and mix a drag of about 100 basis points; mix drag comes from continued post-COVID group-size normalization, rewards free-entree redemptions, slight BYOC cannibalization and snack-occasion items like protein cups and single tacos, partly offset by extra meat from the protein campaign and sauces (Red Chimichurri, then Cilantro Lime). Mix should be closer to flat in Q2 thanks to the Cilantro Lime Sauce check benefit, with the second half depending on protein LTO pricing and sauces. Scott: customers are more discerning and want hospitality more than at any time since COVID; Jason Kidd's team rallied at the All Managers Conference around treating guests like guests in your home, and it is showing in better staffing KPIs, the best apprentice model levels in years, GM turnover at historical lows and rising taste of food and guest satisfaction scores, with pockets of opportunity remaining.

exchanges.question: Given a price-perception issue over the last year or two, how much will value and price points be integrated into the marketing message under Fernando, and how much has he been tasked with that?
exchanges.answer: Chipotle is open to testing many ideas and will not handicap Fernando with entrenched thinking, but will do nothing that detracts from brand health. Scott believes the price point is very fair; Chipotle has underpriced the industry for a second consecutive year and sits at a 20%-30% discount to fast casual peers with the gap widening year over year, building pricing power to pull when the timing is right. Levers include entry-level price points like the $3.50 high-protein taco and a Happier Hour test in one market in a couple of weeks with tacos at $2.50 from two to five, to learn where pricing elasticity exists and make guests feel they get extraordinary value.

exchanges.question: Are transaction growth gaps converging between the previously pressured younger and lower-to-middle income cohorts and the rest of the customer base? Follow-up: where do European unit economics (AUVs, middle of the P&L) stand and is Europe at an inflection point to accelerate unit growth?
exchanges.answer: Targeted messaging and culturally relevant moments engaged younger consumers more in Q1 than over the last year, and there was an uptick across all ages and income cohorts; management knows which levers engage each cohort and is confident the Recipe for Growth strategy will keep moving them up. Europe is absolutely at an inflection: margins are now in the double-digit range and new restaurants are delivering 40% ROI in year two (he first misspoke as 40% new restaurant growth), so Chipotle needs to look for real estate more meaningfully in Central London and Germany and is released to go as quickly as it can.

exchanges.question: With competition growing in chicken, Mexican and bowl concepts, is there an opportunity to market locally where competitors are growing rather than only nationally? And did new unit volumes come in a touch light in Q1 versus expectations, or were timing factors involved?
exchanges.answer: A deep dive on New York and Florida, where the fastest-growing (still small) competitors are, shows some cannibalization in the first six months or so after a competitor opens near a Chipotle, with recovery in months six, seven and eight and a return to Chipotle trends; competitor openings bring more consumers to the trade area, which buoys long-term performance, and the impact today is low though monitored. Marketing dollars work hardest at the national level, so bifurcating spend to attack locally would be costly and likely not the most efficient use. Adam: new restaurant productivity is about 80% of comp restaurants, where it has been for the last couple of years; Q1 openings were pushed later in the quarter rather than evenly spread, which likely explains the analyst's calculation.

exchanges.question: Is the delivery premium an area to explore for improving the lower value scores in the delivery channel? Follow-up: where do store labor levels need to settle, is Chipotle fully staffed, or is there more opportunity to invest?
exchanges.answer: Chipotle tested different delivery premiums on DoorDash and Uber: consumers use Uber as a discount platform and DoorDash as a premium, faster platform, requiring different marketing; even at elevated marketplace prices Chipotle remains below peers in the channel. Delivery ticked up again last quarter (still in the teens) and order-ahead surpassed 20% in the quarter as consumers choose pickup; Arlie Sisson starts next week and will take a hard look at third-party aggregators, using last year's tests to shape the back-half go-to-market. On labor there is more opportunity to invest: hours freed by HEAP (an incremental couple of hours), Chipotle Kitchen, the GM Assistant and Ava Cado are reinvested in the business rather than taken out, and management complement is being reworked so a manager covers all 14 peaks (lunch and dinner every day, including Saturday and Sunday), which is a challenge today that Jason's team is executing a plan against.

exchanges.question: What is the shape of restaurant margins into the second half as the pricing-inflation gap narrows, and what comp or traffic is needed to see expansion exiting the year? Follow-up: has the HEAP comp gap versus control widened in early restaurants, and what is the rollout pace to reach 2,000 by year-end?
exchanges.answer: The first half carries the most year-over-year margin pressure: Q1 pricing of 0.9% against inflation in the mid 3% range is the main dislocation; in the second half inflation drops as elevated beef prices are lapped and pricing ticks up under the slow, measured approach, so the dislocation should be minimal by year-end, after which margin gains come from price offsetting inflation plus incremental transactions. Scott: HEAP restaurants outperform on throughput, taste of food, OSAT and comp lift of 200-400 basis points depending on the restaurant; Chipotle is at 600 restaurants today and will reach 2,000 by year-end, moving from about 30-35 installs per week this quarter to 45 per week in the next month or so, installing overnight without closing restaurants and allowing about a month for teams to get up to speed; the full portfolio should be done late 2027 or early 2028.

exchanges.question: How long after deploying the HEAP package does the same-store sales improvement appear? Follow-up: marketing spend grew about 22% in Q1 after a heavy Q4 yet the marginal comp lift looks modest; how is the incremental return measured and is conversion strong enough to justify this spend level?
exchanges.answer: About two months: roughly a month to become proficient and another to hit stride, after which material uplift appears. Adam: the spend supporting four LTOs and Chipotle days such as the tattoo BOGO is earning good incremental returns, each measured individually, though consumer noise remains and returns are expected to keep improving. Scott: marketing has a tail, with the goal being sales overnight and brand over time, and spend will continue to grow incrementally as long as return on ad spend is responsible and margin accretive.

exchanges.question: The Q2 comp guide of +1% versus Q1's +0.5% matches the 50 basis point step-up in price, and with mix moving from -1% to flat, why does Q2 embed a roughly 50 basis point traffic decline unless the guide is as conservative as the full-year outlook? Follow-up: the sustainability report showed a large pickup in hourly turnover in 2025 after three years of declines; what drove it and what are the plans to improve throughput beyond HEAP?
exchanges.answer: The read is right: the guide is modest on the lift expected from Chipotle Honey Chicken and other planned initiatives given the consumer environment, the Iran conflict and gas prices; management is cautious but believes there is upside from there. Scott: the 2025 hourly turnover rise was an anomaly as sales decelerated and hours fell, driving attrition, and the hospitality focus prompted hard decisions about crew who were not naturally friendly; Q1 2026 turnover is back to historical lows. The throughput-beyond-HEAP part was not addressed and the analyst did not press it.

guidance.current: About flat (unchanged); trending higher than guidance but kept conservative given the dynamic consumer environment
